To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the micro-heterogenity of the alcohol-water and alcohol-alkane mixtures is best described by a correlation function analysis, which reveals a clear structure factor signature.

(i) the structure factor is more efficient than the cluster distribution analysis to describe micro-heterogeneous mixtures, since it detects the domain structure, which is the more fundamental statistical entity; (ii) the structure factor pre- peak is more pronounced in mixtures with water, because the alcohol-water interaction is stronger, and the alcohol-alcohol interaction is weaker, than the alcohol-alkane interaction; and (iii) the structure factor and correlation function analysis can detect the micro-segregated structure

the micro-heterogeneous mixtures are characterized by: 1) the presence of a domain pre-peak in the structure factor; 2) the absence of any pre-peak in cluster distribution analysis; 3) the existence of an intermediate range correlation in the correlation function; and 4) the presence of two length scales in the correlation function, which are the cluster sizes and the domain size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a fundamental issue of physical chemistry: the structure of mixtures.

the statistical description of the morphological changes in binary mixtures, with the emphasis on the micro-heterogeneous regime, and on the comparison of the different statistical techniques that can be used to describe these changes.
the statistical description of the morphological changes in the mixtures of alcohols with water or alcohols with alkanes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the micro-heterogeneous mixtures of ethanol in alkanes or water are best understood by the correlation function/structural factor analysis, while the cluster analysis is better suited to the study of neat liquids, where no micro-heterogeneity is present.
the domain structure is the more fundamental statistical entity, while the cluster structures are the more fundamental morphological entities.

, in micro-heterogeneous mixtures, the cluster distribution analysis is a useful but not a fundamental technique, while the correlation function/ structure factor analysis is a fundamental and heuristic tool.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure factor and the correlation function are complementary to the cluster distribution function, and should be used together to understand micro-heterogeneity.

micro-heterogeneity in binary mixtures is a phenomenon of domains rather than clusters, and that the structure factor is a more fundamental descriptor of micro-heterogeneity than the cluster distribution function.
micro-heterogeneity in alcohol mixtures is a consequence of clustering in the alcohol-rich regions, but that the domain structure is more fundamental than the underlying clustering structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the micro-segregation of ethanol with water and alkanes is a very different phenomenon, and this is reflected by the different evolution of the structure factor pre- peak.

, in the case of mixtures with micro-heterogeneity (i.e., micro-segregation), the domain size is the relevant statistical length scale, while in the case of clustering, the relevant length scale is the cluster size.

, in order to better characterize the micro-heterogeneous mixtures, the correlation function/ structure factor analysis should be used as a primary tool, while the cluster distribution analysis is used as a complementary tool.
